summary: This is a 17-page NIH R01-style research plan (5 years, modular budget) proposing to develop and prospectively validate an extracellular vesicle (EV) proteomic panel measured by mass spectrometry as a triage test applied after a positive faecal immunochemical test (FIT) and before colonoscopy for colorectal cancer (CRC) screening. The project is at an early research/concept stage (TRL 1–2), with no experimental data yet generated; all quantitative claims are derived from literature meta-analysis of 131 FIT-triage and 56 EV-proteomics records. The plan is structured around three stage-gated aims: assay development (Years 1–2), biomarker discovery and panel lock (Years 2–3), and prospective blinded validation in N=2,000 consecutive FIT-positive adults (Years 3–5).

content_blocks.title: Specific Aims — Overview and Clinical Problem
content_blocks.content: Organised CRC screening with FIT refers every test-positive participant to colonoscopy. Across 22 retrieved cohorts: median probability of CRC after positive FIT = 5.1% (IQR 3.15–8.0%); median probability of any advanced neoplasm = 21.1% (IQR 16.9–33.0%). Roughly 4 in 5 colonoscopies triggered by positive FIT find nothing requiring colonoscopy. Median serious-complication rate = 3.13 per 1,000 procedures (13 retrieved reports). Proposal: develop and prospectively validate an EV proteomic panel by mass spectrometry as a triage test after positive FIT and before colonoscopy.

content_blocks.title: Aim 1 — Assay Development and Pre-analytical Lock (Years 1–2)
content_blocks.content: Compare size-exclusion chromatography (SEC), ultracentrifugation (UC), and tetraspanin (CD9/CD63/CD81) immunoaffinity capture head-to-head on FIT-positive plasmas. Characterise every isolate to MISEV2023 standards (NTA, TEM, immunoblot for tetraspanins + calnexin negative marker). Qualify DIA mass-spectrometry workflow. Gate 1: ≥1,500 proteins at median CV ≤30% from ≤1 mL plasma, stable across pre-analytical stress panel. Rationale: retrieved literature median depth = 826 proteins from 0.8 mL plasma; only 4 of 56 EV studies used DIA.

content_blocks.title: Aim 2 — Discovery and Panel Lock (Years 2–3)
content_blocks.content: Unbiased DIA-MS discovery on retrospective FIT-positive biobank: n=50 advanced neoplasia, n=50 neoplasia-free colonoscopy (frequency-matched on age, sex, site). Two sites, randomised block injection order, site as model covariate. Panel reduction: nested cross-validated elastic net to ≤12 proteins + 2 EV normalisers. Transfer to targeted PRM with heavy stable-isotope-labelled internal standards. Gate 2: locked panel, locked coefficients, locked single threshold, held-out AUC ≥0.80. Controls are FIT-positive patients with negative colonoscopy — not healthy donors.

content_blocks.title: Aim 3 — Prospective Blinded Validation (Years 3–5)
content_blocks.content: Enrol N=2,000 consecutive FIT-positive adults across 4 endoscopy units in 2 integrated health systems. Blood drawn before bowel preparation. Locked PRM panel run blinded to endoscopic outcome. Reference standard: colonoscopy with central histopathology adjudication. At retrieved prevalence priors: 422 advanced neoplasms and 102 cancers expected. Gate 3 (co-primary): CRC sensitivity ≥98% AND advanced-neoplasia NPV ≥95% at single pre-specified threshold. Exclusions: prior CRC, IBD, colonoscopy within 5 years, inability to complete colonoscopy within 6 months.

content_blocks.title: Co-primary Endpoint Rationale and Decision Analysis Preview
content_blocks.content: Both criteria (≤1 missed cancer per 1,000 FIT-positive patients AND advanced-neoplasia NPV ≥95%) are satisfied at only 10 of 203 operating points evaluated, and only where CRC sensitivity ≥98.2% meets specificity ≥86% simultaneously. Either criterion alone is far easier than the pair. The trial is designed to fail honestly rather than produce a publishable AUC regardless of clinical value.

content_blocks.title: Section 2.1 — The Unnecessary-Colonoscopy Burden
content_blocks.content: From fit_triage_evidence.csv (131 extracted records): median FIT sensitivity for CRC = 80% (IQR 69.0–89.6%); median specificity = 91%; median programme positivity = 7.65% (IQR 5.0–13.02%). Largest single retrieved cohort: organised biennial programme, 2.81 million invitations, 2010–2023 (PMID 41617486), reports CRC PPV = 5.10%, advanced neoplasia PPV = 20.40%. Of every 1,000 colonoscopies on FIT-positive participants, ~790 find no advanced neoplasm, carrying ~3.1 serious complications.

content_blocks.title: Section 2.2 — Triage vs. Screening Positioning
content_blocks.content: In a screening population, advanced neoplasia prevalence ~1%; after positive FIT, prevalence = 21.1% (20-fold higher). This enrichment: (1) makes high NPV attainable at achievable specificity; (2) shrinks required validation cohort from tens of thousands to 2,000; (3) defines a clean comparator (colonoscopy in same patients). This is the key strategic positioning of the proposal.

content_blocks.title: Section 2.3 — Competitive Landscape: Pivotal Blood/Stool CRC Trials
content_blocks.content:
From crc_blood_test_landscape.csv (116 trials; 88 blood-based). Key pivotal programmes:
- NCT04369053 (Freenome): n=48,995, multiomics blood, average-risk screening
- NCT04136002 (Guardant Health): n=44,467, ctDNA, average-risk screening
- NCT04144738 BLUE-C (Exact Sciences): n=26,758, multi-target stool DNA, average-risk screening
- NCT04739722 (Geneoscopy): n=14,263, stool RNA, average-risk screening
- NCT06059963 (Universal Diagnostics): n=12,000, blood, average-risk screening
- NCT00855348 PRESEPT (Epigenomics): n=7,929, methylated SEPT9, average-risk screening
Registry holds 13 EV-related CRC trials; largest is NCT06342401 (n=400, City of Hope) for early-onset detection. No retrieved trial evaluates EV proteomic panel for FIT triage at any scale.

content_blocks.title: Section 3 — Innovation Points
content_blocks.content: Five innovation claims: (1) Controls in discovery and validation are FIT-positive patients with neoplasia-free colonoscopy — not healthy donors — avoiding pre-analytical and demographic confounding. (2) Safety constraint is a co-primary endpoint computed in advance from decision analysis. (3) Precision (CV), not sample size, is the gated parameter; Gate 1 is a CV gate. (4) Capture handles and readout analytes separated on structural grounds: only EPCAM, EGFR, MET, CD44 have integral TM segment with defined ectodomain — prerequisite for immunocapture ligand. (5) Contamination-prone candidates (SERPINA3, FGA — high-abundance hepatic plasma proteins) excluded a priori as Tier 3.

content_blocks.title: Figure 1 — Three-Aim Workflow with Stage Gates
content_blocks.content: Diagram showing the three-aim workflow with three stage gates and pre-specified failure branch. Aim 1 (Y1-Y2): Multi-site plasma collection SOP → EV isolation head-to-head (SEC vs UC vs immunocapture) → MISEV2023 characterisation (NTA, TEM, CD9/CD63/CD81, calnexin-negative) → DIA-MS depth & precision (≥1,500 proteins, median CV ≤30%) → Pre-analytical stress panel (delay, F/T, haemolysis). Gate 1 at end Y2. Aim 2 (Y2-Y3): Retrospective FIT-positive biobank (n=50 advanced neoplasia, n=50 no neoplasia) → DIA-MS discovery (n=25/group/site, 2 sites, randomised block injection order) → Differential abundance (limma on log2, BH-FDR 5%, site as covariate) → Panel reduction (nested-CV elastic net, locked to ≤12 proteins + 2 EV normalisers) → PRM/MRM transfer with heavy peptides (LLOQ, linearity, inter-lab CV ≤20%). Gate 2 mid Y3. Aim 3 (Y3-Y5): Prospective enrolment at 4 FIT-programme sites, N=2,000 consecutive FIT-positive adults → Blood drawn BEFORE bowel preparation → Reference standard: colonoscopy + histology, central pathology adjudication → Pre-specified analysis: sens/spec/NPV at locked threshold, STARD reporting → Decision model: colonoscopies avoided, cancers missed, cost per case detected. Gate 3 at end Y5: CRC sensitivity ≥98% AND AN NPV ≥95%. Pre-specified failure branch: if Gate 2 not met, Aim 3 converts to confirmatory single-marker design on highest-ranked capture-tractable target (EPCAM or EGFR ectodomain).

content_blocks.title: Section 4.1 — Aim 1 Detailed Design
content_blocks.content: EV evidence table (ev_proteomics_crc_evidence.csv, 56 studies, 51 in CRC): median total N=100, median depth 826 proteins, median input 0.8 mL, DIA used in 4 studies. Only 15 of 51 CRC studies report any independent validation. Several report AUCs at or approaching 1.00 in cohorts of a few dozen — pattern characteristic of overfitting. Design: 30 FIT-positive plasmas split three ways (SEC, UC, CD9/CD63/CD81 immunoaffinity). Single locked SOP: K₂EDTA, two-step centrifugation, ≤2h draw-to-freeze. DIA on high-field orbitrap with project-specific spectral library; pooled reference every 10 samples. Pre-analytical stress panel: draw-to-freeze delay (2/4/8/24h), 1–3 freeze-thaw cycles, graded haemolysis and lipaemia. Any protein moving more under pre-analytical variation than disease is disqualified before Gate 2.

content_blocks.title: Section 4.2 — Candidate Protein Watchlist (14 proteins)
content_blocks.content:
14 proteins replicated across ≥2 independent EV-CRC studies, annotated from UniProt (human, reviewed):

Tier 1:
- OLFM4: 3 studies, secreted/soluble, high intestinal/goblet specificity, quantified analyte only
- CEA: 3 studies, peripheral/membrane-associated (no ectodomain), high colonic epithelium, quantified analyte only
- EPCAM: 3 studies, integral TM + defined ectodomain, pan-epithelial, capture ligand candidate + quantified analyte
- EGFR: 3 studies, integral TM + defined ectodomain, broad epithelial, capture ligand candidate + quantified analyte

Tier 2:
- MET: 2 studies, integral TM + defined ectodomain, broad epithelial, capture ligand candidate + quantified analyte
- S100A9: 2 studies, peripheral/membrane-associated (no ectodomain), myeloid (neutrophil), quantified analyte only
- CD44: 2 studies, integral TM + defined ectodomain, broad, capture ligand candidate + quantified analyte
- MYH9: 2 studies, peripheral/membrane-associated (no ectodomain), ubiquitous, quantified analyte only
- LGALS3BP: 3 studies, secreted/soluble, broad, quantified analyte only

Tier 3 (excluded from locked panel a priori):
- SERPINA3: 2 studies, secreted/soluble, hepatic (plasma), quantified analyte only
- ANXA11: 2 studies, cytosolic/lumenal, ubiquitous, quantified analyte only
- ANXA5: 2 studies, cytosolic/lumenal, ubiquitous, quantified analyte only
- FGA: 2 studies, secreted/soluble, hepatic (plasma), quantified analyte only
- GSTP1: 2 studies, cytosolic/lumenal, broad, quantified analyte only

content_blocks.title: Section 4.3 — Aim 3 Detailed Design
content_blocks.content: Population: consecutive adults with positive FIT in organised screening at 4 endoscopy units across 2 integrated health systems, enrolled over 21 months, N=2,000. Blood drawn at pre-colonoscopy visit before bowel preparation. Exclusions: prior CRC, IBD, colonoscopy within 5 years, inability to complete colonoscopy within 6 months. Reference standard: full colonoscopy with histopathology of all resected lesions, adjudicated centrally and blinded to panel results. Advanced neoplasia defined as: CRC, or adenoma ≥10mm, or high-grade dysplasia, or ≥25% villous component, or sessile serrated lesion ≥10mm. Measurement: locked PRM panel, monthly batches, randomised case-control-balanced injection order, blinded to endoscopic outcome, pooled reference QC every 10 samples, batch as pre-specified covariate. Analysis: primary sensitivity/specificity/NPV/PPV at locked threshold with exact Clopper-Pearson CIs; secondary AUC, stratified performance, incremental value over quantitative FIT haemoglobin. Reporting: STARD with complete flow diagram.

content_blocks.title: Figure 2 — Statistical Design and Power Simulations
content_blocks.content: Three panels: (a) Simulated discovery power: fraction of truly differential proteins recovered at BH-FDR 5% across 1,000-protein panel, by group size and analytical CV. At n=25/group: 2.0× fold change at CV 30% = 100% recovery; 1.5× at CV 30% = 99%; 1.5× at CV 40% = 84%; 1.3× at CV 20% = 97%; 1.3× at CV 30% = 58%. (b) Validation precision as function of total cohort size at retrieved prevalence priors — sensitivity claim (not AUC) sets cohort size. (c) Achieved power for pre-specified sensitivity floors at locked cohort size (N=2,000): AN sensitivity >85% floor at 90% true = 91% power; AN sensitivity >85% at 92.5% true = 99.9%; CRC sensitivity >85% at 95% true = 97%; CRC sensitivity >90% at 98% true = 95%; CRC sensitivity >90% at 95% true = 42% (honest limit).

content_blocks.title: Section 5.1 — Discovery Power: CV is the Binding Constraint
content_blocks.content:
Simulated two-sample comparisons on log₂ intensities across 1,000-protein panel with 5% truly differential, BH control at 5%, at n=25 per group:
- 2.0× fold change, CV 30%: 100% recovery
- 1.5× fold change, CV 30%: 99% recovery; CV 40%: 84%
- 1.3× fold change, CV 20%: 97%; CV 30%: 58%
Dropping CV from 30% to 20% raises 1.3-fold recovery from 58% to 97% — larger gain than any affordable increase in N. Effects below 1.3-fold declared out of scope. This is why Gate 1 is a precision gate.

content_blocks.title: Section 5.2 — Validation Power Table
content_blocks.content:
At N=2,000 with prevalence priors (21.1% advanced neoplasia, 5.1% CRC): 422 advanced neoplasms, 102 cancers, 1,578 neoplasia-free. Sensitivity power (binomial, Clopper-Pearson one-sided lower bound, α=0.05):
- AN sensitivity, 422 cases, true 90%, floor >85%: 91% power
- AN sensitivity, 422 cases, true 92.5%, floor >85%: 99.9% power
- CRC sensitivity, 102 cases, true 95%, floor >85%: 97% power
- CRC sensitivity, 102 cases, true 98%, floor >90%: 95% power
- CRC sensitivity, 102 cases, true 95%, floor >90%: 42% power (honest limit)
Precision at N=2,000: AUC half-width ±0.024 (AN) and ±0.047 (CRC); sensitivity half-width ±2.9 pp (AN) and ±5.8 pp (CRC).

content_blocks.title: Figure 3 — Decision Analysis: Operating Surface and Admissible Region
content_blocks.content: Three panels: (a) Operating surface showing colonoscopies avoided (fill) with contours for cancers missed and hatched admissible region. Admissibility starts at 98% CRC sensitivity paired with 86% specificity — needs both at once. (b) Advanced adenomas (not cancers) cap the achievable rule-out NPV; 95% NPV target line shown. (c) Absolute counts at nominated operating point (98% CRC sensitivity, 78% advanced-adenoma sensitivity, 60% specificity) per 1,000 FIT-positive patients: colonoscopies performed=490, colonoscopies avoided=510 (51%), advanced neoplasms missed=36, cancers missed=1.0, NPV for advanced neoplasia=92.9%, serious complications averted=1.6. Error bars span IQR of retrieved prevalence (CRC 3.2–8.0%, AN 16.9–33.0%). Colonoscopy complication rate 3.13 per 1,000.

content_blocks.title: Section 6 — Decision Analysis Results Table
content_blocks.content:
Modelled panel applied to 1,000 FIT-positive patients at nominated operating point (98% CRC sensitivity, 78% advanced-adenoma sensitivity, 60% specificity):
- Colonoscopies performed: 490 (range 471–541)
- Colonoscopies avoided: 510 (51%) (range 529–459)
- Cancers missed: 1.0 (range 0.6–1.6)
- Advanced neoplasms missed: 36 (range 31–57)
- NPV for advanced neoplasia: 92.9% (range 94–88%)
- Serious complications averted: 1.6 (range 1.7–1.4)
Key finding: imposing both criteria (≤1 cancer missed per 1,000 AND AN NPV ≥95%) leaves only 10 of 203 grid points admissible, requiring CRC sensitivity ≥98.2% AND specificity ≥86% simultaneously. Advanced adenomas dominate the false-negative pool (4× more prevalent than cancers among FIT-positive patients).

content_blocks.title: Section 7 — Rigour and Reproducibility Measures
content_blocks.content: Blinding: lab staff blinded to endoscopic outcome; endoscopists/pathologists blinded to panel results; statisticians blinded until database lock. Pre-registration: Aim 3 protocol, panel composition, coefficients, threshold and analysis plan registered publicly and deposited with DSMB before first prospective sample drawn. No panel/threshold modification permitted after Gate 2. Randomisation: injection order randomised in balanced blocks within monthly batches; batch and site are pre-specified covariates; pooled reference QC every 10 injections with pre-specified drift rules. Biological variables: sex reported separately; age, site, quantitative FIT concentration are pre-specified covariates. Data/code: raw and processed MS data deposited in ProteomeXchange/PRIDE; analysis code version-controlled and released. Reporting: STARD; EV work reports to MISEV2023 and registered in EV-TRACK.

content_blocks.title: Section 8 — Pre-specified Failure Branches
content_blocks.content:
Pre-specified contingency table:
- Gate 1 fails on depth: Switch to immunocapture-only isolates; accept shallower vesicle-specific proteome; re-baseline panel size; report depth limit as finding.
- Gate 1 fails on CV: Do not proceed to discovery. Reallocate Year 3 to precision engineering; reduce discovery to Tier 1 watchlist measured by PRM.
- Gate 2 fails (no panel reaches AUC 0.80): Aim 3 converts to confirmatory single-marker design on highest-ranked capture-tractable target (EPCAM or EGFR ectodomain), powered for advanced-neoplasia sensitivity alone; panel co-primary dropped and reported as negative result.
- Gate 3 misses rule-out bar but reaches rule-in point: Report negative rule-out result; pursue pre-specified secondary claim of prioritisation of colonoscopy scheduling for high-score patients (no missed-cancer risk).
- Accrual reaches only ~1,500: Report co-primary at achieved N with exact CIs; do not re-power or extend enrolment selectively.
- Competitor approved for triage specifically: Reposition as reflex test on competitor-positive patients; locked assay and prospective cohort retain value as comparator dataset.

content_blocks.title: Figure 4 — Five-Year Timeline with Stage Gates
content_blocks.content: Sixteen-task Gantt chart over 60 months with three gates at months 24, 42, and 60. Tasks span: Aim 1 (assay development, Y1-Y2), Aim 2 (discovery, Y2-Y3), Aim 3 (validation, Y3-Y5), and cross-cutting activities. Key milestones: Month 9: Locked multi-site pre-analytical SOP; all sites activated. Month 15: EV isolation method selected; MISEV2023 dossier complete. Month 24: Gate 1 — assay qualified (≥1,500 proteins, median CV ≤30%). Month 35: Discovery complete; differential abundance locked. Month 36: First prospective participant enrolled. Month 42: Gate 2 — panel, coefficients and threshold locked; pre-registration filed. Month 57: Enrolment complete (N=2,000). Month 60: Database lock; unblinding; co-primary analysis; Gate 3 — co-primary read-out; decision model; Q-Sub package.

Five performance sites:

content_blocks.title: Section 12 — Required Partnerships (8 total)
content_blocks.content:
Eight partnerships required; three are hard preconditions:
- P1 (Essential — Aim 3): Organised FIT screening programme (integrated health system). Provides consecutive FIT-positive patients with scheduled colonoscopy. Instrument: letter of support + subaward + data use agreement + single-IRB reliance.
- P2 (Essential — Aims 1&2): Proteomics/MS core with DIA capability. Provides orbitrap-class DIA, ~1,000+ protein depth from 1 mL plasma-derived EVs, PRM assay transfer, 5-year instrument stability. Instrument: internal core service agreement with guaranteed instrument time.
- P3 (Essential — reference standard): GI endoscopy and pathology service. Provides index colonoscopy reports, withdrawal times, ADR; blinded central pathology re-read. Instrument: co-investigator appointment + per-case pathology adjudication contract.
- P4 (High — de-risks Aim 2 timeline): Biorepository with FIT-positive plasma and linked colonoscopy outcomes. Instrument: material transfer agreement + honest-broker linkage.
- P5 (Medium — Y4-Y5 translation): CLIA laboratory/assay-development partner. Provides transfer of locked PRM panel into CLIA-validated LDT. Instrument: fee-for-service or co-development agreement.
- P6 (Medium — required for prospective aim): Data safety monitoring board/independent oversight. Instrument: DSMB charter; honoraria budgeted.
- P7 (Medium — rigour): EV methodology/MISEV reporting advisor. Instrument: advisory role, honorarium.
- P8 (Optional — strengthens Aim 3 interpretation): Health-economics/screening-modelling collaborator. Instrument: unfunded collaboration or supplement.
Binding constraint: P1. FIT positivity median 7.65% (IQR 5.00–13.02%); system performing 30,000 FITs/year generates ~2,300 positives/year; two systems accruing over 3 years supports 2,000-participant Aim 3 target.

content_blocks.title: Section 14 — Risk Register (10 risks)
content_blocks.content:
Ten risks with likelihood/impact and mitigations:
- R1 (Analytical, High/High): High-abundance plasma protein co-isolation swamps EV proteome. Mitigation: 3-way isolation comparison, MISEV2023 evidence required, FGA/SERPINA3 pre-assigned Tier 3, Gate 1 CV gate. Contingency: switch to immunocapture-only.
- R2 (Biological, High/High): Published EV CRC markers do not replicate independently. Mitigation: unbiased DIA-MS discovery; shortlist is watchlist only; 2-site discovery with site as covariate. Contingency: fallback to Tier 1 capture-tractable targets.
- R3 (Analytical, High/Medium): Discovery underpowered for modest effects (58% recovery of 1.3-fold at CV 30%). Mitigation: CV ceiling at Gate 1; matched FIT-positive controls remove pre-analytical confounding. Contingency: effects <1.3-fold declared out of scope; if CV=40%, increase N to 40/group.
- R4 (Clinical, Medium/High): FIT-positive accrual falls short of N=2,000. Mitigation: rides on existing organised FIT programme; 4 endoscopy units across 2 systems; monthly monitoring with Year 4 decision point. Contingency: report co-primary at achieved N.
- R5 (Pre-analytical, High/High): Pre-analytical drift across 4 endoscopy units creates site-specific EV proteome signatures. Mitigation: single locked SOP (K₂EDTA, ≤2h draw-to-freeze); dedicated stress panel; haemolysis index and platelet-marker QC on every sample. Contingency: site as covariate; close site if QC failure >10%.
- R6 (Analytical, Medium/High): LC-MS instrument drift over multi-year run. Mitigation: targeted PRM/MRM with heavy SIL internal standards; monthly batches with randomised injection order; pooled reference QC every 10 samples; batch as pre-specified covariate. Contingency: re-injection rules; sensitivity analysis excluding failed batches.
- R7 (Statistical, Medium/High): Threshold or panel re-optimised on validation cohort. Mitigation: panel/coefficients/threshold locked at Gate 2 and deposited with DSMB and public pre-registration before Aim 3 opens; analysts blinded until database lock. Contingency: any post hoc threshold reported as exploratory.
- R8 (Translational, Medium/High): Well-performing panel cannot meet safety bar for rule-out triage. Mitigation: safety constraint pre-specified as co-primary; decision model is named deliverable. Contingency: if misses rule-out but reaches rule-in, pursue colonoscopy scheduling prioritisation claim.
- R9 (Competitive, High/Low): cfDNA or stool-based competitor approved for same indication before Year 5. Mitigation: targets FIT triage (not addressed by pivotal programmes); EV proteome is orthogonal to cfDNA methylation. Contingency: reposition as reflex test.
- R10 (Regulatory, Medium/Low): CLIA and FDA path longer than award period. Mitigation: regulatory support budgeted from Year 4; Q-Sub meeting scheduled on strength of locked assay and enrolled cohort. Contingency: Year 5 deliverable seeds confirmatory study.

content_blocks.title: Section 15 — Honest Appraisal
content_blocks.content: Three candid admissions: (1) The biology is the bet, and the evidence for it is thin. Corpus: 56 EV studies, 51 in CRC, median N=100, only 15 with independent validation. Only 14 proteins recur across ≥2 independent studies; a third are ubiquitous cytoskeletal, annexin, or high-abundance plasma proteins whose presence in EV preparations is as consistent with co-isolation as with tumour-derived cargo. Plan does not assume any published marker replicates. (2) The rule-out bar is harder than the field's published AUCs suggest. Several retrieved studies report AUCs >0.96 in cohorts of a few dozen. Decision analysis shows even 98% cancer sensitivity does not clear 95% advanced-neoplasia NPV unless specificity also reaches ~86%, because advanced adenomas dominate the false-negative pool. (3) The absence of competitors is ambiguous evidence — either an opening or a verdict. Stage-gated structure is the answer: Gate 1 costs 2 years and ~$859,000 to establish whether the assay can be made precise enough to be worth testing.

content_blocks.title: Deliverables — Supporting Data Files
content_blocks.content:
Eight supporting data files:
- fit_triage_evidence.csv: 131 extracted records on FIT programme performance, predictive values, positivity and colonoscopy complications
- ev_proteomics_crc_evidence.csv: 56 EV biomarker studies (51 CRC), methods detail mined from 31 full texts
- crc_blood_test_landscape.csv: 116 registered CRC screening/triage trials classified by modality
- candidate_targets_annotated.csv: 14 replicated candidates with UniProt topology, tissue specificity, tier and panel role
- design_calculations.csv: Discovery power simulations, AUC and exact sensitivity sizing, achieved power at locked N
- decision_analysis.csv: Operating-point grid with admissibility flags and prevalence sensitivity analysis
- budget_summary.csv: Line-item modular budget by year
- risk_register.csv: Ten risks with evidence, mitigation and contingency
Additional files: performance_sites.csv, required_partnerships.csv, advisory_contacts.csv

key_findings: No experimental data have been generated by this team yet; the proposal is a forward-looking research plan grounded in literature meta-analysis.
Across 22 retrieved cohorts, median probability of CRC after a positive FIT is 5.1% (IQR 3.15–8.0%); median probability of any advanced neoplasm is 21.1% (IQR 16.9–33.0%).
Median serious-complication rate of colonoscopy is 3.13 per 1,000 procedures (13 retrieved reports).

Across 56 retrieved EV proteomics studies (51 in CRC): median total N=100, median proteome depth 826 proteins from median 0.8 mL plasma; only 4 of 56 studies used DIA; only 15 of 51 CRC studies report any independent validation.
Only 14 proteins replicated across ≥2 independent EV-CRC studies; a third are ubiquitous cytoskeletal, annexin, or high-abundance plasma proteins potentially representing co-isolation artifacts.
No registered trial evaluates an EV proteomic panel for FIT triage at any scale (registry of 116 CRC trials reviewed).
Gate 1 target: ≥1,500 proteins quantified at median CV ≤30% from ≤1 mL plasma with MISEV2023 compliance.
Gate 2 target: locked panel (≤12 proteins + 2 EV normalisers) with held-out AUC ≥0.80 and inter-laboratory CV ≤20%.
Gate 3 (co-primary): CRC sensitivity ≥98% AND advanced-neoplasia NPV ≥95% at a single pre-specified threshold.
Decision analysis shows that meeting both co-primary criteria requires CRC sensitivity ≥98.2% coinciding with specificity ≥86%; only 10 of 203 operating points evaluated are admissible.

At the nominated operating point (98% CRC sensitivity, 78% advanced-adenoma sensitivity, 60% specificity), per 1,000 FIT-positive patients: 510 colonoscopies avoided (51%), 1.0 cancer missed, 36 advanced neoplasms missed, NPV for advanced neoplasia 92.9%.
Advanced adenomas (not cancers) cap the achievable NPV because they are ~4× more prevalent than cancers among FIT-positive patients.
Discovery power simulations: at n=25/group and CV 30%, 99% recovery of 1.5-fold changes; only 58% recovery of 1.3-fold changes — CV is the binding constraint, not N.
Validation cohort of N=2,000 yields 422 advanced neoplasms and 102 cancers at retrieved prevalence priors; achieves 95% power for CRC sensitivity floor >90% if true sensitivity is 98%.

Candidate protein watchlist of 14 proteins identified; Tier 1 (OLFM4, CEA, EPCAM, EGFR) and Tier 2 (MET, S100A9, CD44, MYH9, LGALS3BP); Tier 3 (SERPINA3, ANXA11, ANXA5, FGA, GSTP1) excluded a priori from locked panel.
EPCAM, EGFR, MET, CD44 are the only candidates with integral transmembrane segment and defined ectodomain — candidate immunocapture ligands.
Total 5-year direct costs: $2,304,000 (total with F&A at 58.5%: $3,651,840); all years below $500,000 direct-cost threshold.
Eight required partnerships identified; three are hard preconditions (organised FIT programme, DIA-capable MS core, GI endoscopy/pathology service).
